stem: What is the relationship between sleep duration and risk-taking behavior in adolescents?

options.text: Reduced sleep impairs prefrontal cortex function and self-regulation.
Lack of sleep increases motor coordination, encouraging physical risks.
Risk-taking is only associated with excessive sleep, not sleep restriction.
There is no established link between brain function and sleep in this age group.

explanation: Poor sleep limits the ability of the prefrontal cortex to govern impulses, leading to higher rates of risk-taking.
rationale: Identify which part of the brain is responsible for impulse control.

optionExplanations.A: Poor sleep limits the ability of the prefrontal cortex to govern impulses, leading to higher rates of risk-taking.
optionExplanations.B: Sleep deprivation significantly impairs motor coordination rather than increasing it.
optionExplanations.C: The association is specifically between low sleep duration/quality and increased risk-taking.
optionExplanations.D: The role of the prefrontal cortex in learning, memory, and self-regulation is well-established in sleep research.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: Reduced sleep impairs prefrontal cortex function and self-regulation.
